rules: Reference fixture lead names, company values, blocker rows, dates and counts are never copied into runtime state or submitted to the API.
Current lead, client, case and workspace IDs are read from existing runtime owners and preserved in task/activity scope.
Missing/blocker records use the existing linked task/activity source of truth; case_items are not a parallel active store.
Unsupported bulk reminder is disabled with truthful copy because the current runtime has no safe supported endpoint.
Every semantic color resolves from canonical --cf-vst-* token owners; reference-image discrepancies never create per-screen color exceptions.
The delete semantic base is --cf-vst-color-delete; strong, soft and border variants derive from it, and every trash icon resolves to that family.
No fake success, no-op persistence model, automatic merge, silent fallback, unapproved browser mutation or production merge was introduced.

color_source_of_truth.policy: One semantic concern maps to one VST token owner across every window and repeated component instance; all trash/delete icons share the same semantic delete family.

visible_controls_wired: Every visible supported control is wired to an existing owner: add opens the real missing-item form; resolve-all iterates current open items; the blocker checkbox persists supported priority plus task/activity state; edit opens the existing task editor; resolve writes done/resolved state and activity; delete confirms, optimistically updates only the scoped list and preserves the committed server soft-delete; CSV exports current runtime rows; history routes to the existing LeadDetail activity tab. The bulk reminder is explicitly disabled because its backend capability is absent.
backend_boundary: The task PATCH route strips unsupported missing_item status values, so blocker toggle persistence uses the supported high/medium priority field while preserving the existing missing_item type. DELETE is a verified server soft-delete. Activity history is best effort after a committed mutation and never causes a committed delete to reappear locally. Client relation checks fail closed and server workspace/owner scoping remains authoritative.
